title: Inheritance
description: Let one class reuse the attributes and methods of another class.

content.value: Suppose you have an `Animal` class with a `name` and an `eat()` method. Now you want a `Dog` class that has all of that, plus a `bark()` method. Instead of copying the shared code, you can have `Dog` inherit from `Animal`. Inheriting means the new class automatically gets everything the other class has.
You put the parent class name in parentheses when you define the child class. The child gets the parent's attributes and methods, and can add its own on top.
Even though `Dog` has no `eat` method of its own, it inherited one from `Animal`. So you can call `eat()` on a dog and it just works, alongside its own `bark()`.

my_dog = Dog("Buddy")
my_dog.eat()   # Prints: Buddy is eating!
my_dog.bark()  # Prints: Buddy says Woof!

practice.question: Make a Dog object named 'rover' (Dog inherits from Animal) and call its eat() method.

quiz.question: What does a child class get through inheritance?
options: It gets the parent class's attributes and methods.
quiz.explain: A child class automatically gets (inherits) all the attributes and methods of its parent, then can add its own.

quiz.question: How do you define a class 'Car' that inherits from 'Vehicle'?
quiz.explain: You put the parent's name in parentheses: `class Car(Vehicle):` means Car inherits from Vehicle.
